description: Add bilateral mild pitting edema of the lower extremities
presentation: An 82-year-old male with a history of HTN, HLD, CAD, CKD, and prostate cancer metastasized to the lungs presents with acute onset pain, stiffness, swelling, and redness of the hands and feet. Symptoms began with pain and progressed to stiffness, swelling, and tenderness by the 5th day. He was recently started on pantoprazole but symptoms began before that. He is taking capecitabine daily and receiving oxaliplatin infusions every three weeks for chemotherapy. On exam, he has swelling of his digits, significant cracking and dry skin, particularly on the toes and plantar foot, pink coloration of the palms and soles, and bilateral mild pitting edema of the lower extremities. Should I start oral prednisone?
